questions.title: The amniotic cavity and the epiblast
questions.question: Which of the following cavities is directly covered and roofed by the epiblast layer during early embryonic development?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The primitive yolk sac cavity is bounded by the hypoblast, not the epiblast.
explanations.B: Correct. On the eighth day, the embryoblast splits into epiblast and hypoblast, and a cavity opens within the remainder of the inner cell mass — the amniotic cavity. The epiblast forms the floor of this cavity, while the amnioblast (flat cells in contact with the cytotrophoblast) forms its roof. The amniotic cavity is therefore the cavity the epiblast bounds during early embryonic development.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The extraembryonic chorionic cavity forms later, around day 13, from spaces in the extraembryonic mesoderm, and is not bounded by the epiblast.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The blastocyst cavity (blastocele) is the fluid-filled cavity of the earlier blastocyst stage, bounded by trophoblast and hypoblast, not specifically by the epiblast.

questions.title: The epiblast as the floor of the amniotic cavity
questions.question: During early embryonic development the epiblast layer directly covers and forms the floor of which fluid filled cavity?

options.A: The primary primitive yolk sac cavity

explanations.A: Incorrect. The primitive yolk sac cavity is bounded by the hypoblast, not the epiblast.
explanations.B: Correct. The embryoblast splits into epiblast and hypoblast on the eighth day, and the cavity that opens above the epiblast — the amniotic cavity — is roofed by the amnioblast while the epiblast itself forms its floor. This precise floor/roof assignment is the standard teaching point tested by this stem.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The blastocyst cavity (blastocele) is the fluid-filled cavity of the earlier blastocyst stage, bounded by trophoblast and hypoblast, not specifically formed with the epiblast as its floor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The extraembryonic chorionic cavity forms later, around day 13, from spaces in the extraembryonic mesoderm, and is not the cavity the epiblast forms the floor of.

questions.title: The cloacal membrane closes the distal hindgut
questions.question: During embryonic folding the distal end of the developing hind gut is effectively closed by which specific structure?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The chorionic membrane is part of the extraembryonic membranes surrounding the developing embryo, not the structure closing the distal hindgut.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Heuser's membrane is a temporary layer from the hypoblast that forms the wall of the primary yolk sac early in the second week, not the structure closing the distal hindgut.
explanations.C: Correct. The cloacal membrane is a bilaminar (ectoderm+endoderm, no intervening mesoderm) membrane at the caudal end of the embryonic disc. During embryonic folding, it closes off the distal end of the developing hindgut (the cloaca) until it later ruptures to establish the definitive anal and urogenital openings.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The extraembryonic mesodermal covering is a supporting layer of the extraembryonic membranes, not the specific bilaminar structure closing the distal hindgut.
